preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI-enabled system treats permission to access, inspect, analyse, or act within a workspace as implicit permission to copy, bundle, transmit, replicate, persist, index, retain, train on, or otherwise reuse data from that workspace beyond the minimum scope required for the authorised task. The failure includes undisclosed repository-scale transfer, transfer of files not inspected or required, inclusion of deleted history or ignored files, inaccurate representation of privacy controls, and absence of a purpose-bound egress manifest.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met when data materially exceeding the requested or necessary task scope leaves the governed environment; when read authority is silently converted into transmission, persistence, training, or secondary-use authority; when the user cannot determine destination, scope, purpose, retention, or deletion status; or when a privacy or model-improvement control is represented as an egress control despite not preventing transmission.

known_limitations: This pass reviewed canonical record evidence and repository state; it did not independently re-open every external primary source.
Severity was bounded to the evidenced failure definition, harm pathway, deployment scope, recurrence, and stated uncertainty.
Legacy priority values were not treated as model 2.0 historical transitions because their prior semantic basis was not consistently evidenced.
